0.description: Value carried into an analysis from the procedure, where the entry is a spec.
Human-readable label, matching the TAPP Metadata Item where one exists.
URI(s) identifying this property in a vocabulary. Always an array of IRI-reference objects where present; left unconstrained here because the profiles that care already constrain it.
Unit the value is expressed in, as written.
The value. Left untyped on purpose: measured as string, integer and number across the examples, and a technique profile is the right place to pin one.
Machine-readable name, for serialization and form binding.

1.description: Optional geographic extent using wkt geometry, see Ocean InfoHub (https://book.oceaninfohub.org/thematics/spatial/README.html#simple-geosparql-wkt). Other geometry schemes might be specified in a specific domain profile, e.g. for atmospheric, subsurface data, or local coordinate systems. NOTE that the location specified here should be the same as the schema.org point or contained within the specified bounding box.
identifier string for coordinate reference system, e.g., 'CRS84'
Domain-specific type classifications for this place (e.g. facility type,laboratory classification, feature type).

1.title: Laboratory Alternate Name
1.description: Alternate or abbreviated name(s) for this place.
Either a bounding box or a point location.

A GeoShape box defines an area on the surface of the earth defined by point locations of the southwest corner and northeast corner of the rectangle in latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The two corner coordinate points are separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian.

A GeoShape box defines a curvilinear geometry as a string of latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The coordinate point pairs are also separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian. e.g. '39.33 120.77 40.44 123.96 41.00 121.34'

1.title: Laboratory Identifier
1.description: Formal identifier for this place (e.g. ROR identifier for a facility).
A place name for the location, either as a string or a DefinedTerm from a gazetteer.

2.description: identifier for a temporal reference system; default is million years before prsent as a decimal number

3.description: the date of the instant, as an xsd:date

4.title: Assessment Method
4.description: How the statistic was assessed -- repeat measurement of a secondary standard, replicate digestions, counting statistics. Currently bundled into the workbook item name; see the note above.

4.title: Confidence Level
4.description: The confidence interval the value is quoted at, e.g. "1 sigma", "2 sigma", "95%". A string rather than an enum because the corpus has not been surveyed for its spellings; a vocabulary belongs here once it has.

4.title: Measured Standard
4.description: The standard this statistic was measured against, as a reference INTO the procedure's standards table (ada:standardTemplate) rather than a restatement of the material. An accuracy figure without the standard behind it cannot be compared with another lab's.

4.title: Measurement Scope
4.description: Over what span the statistic was assessed. Within-session reproducibility and between-session (long-term) reproducibility are different claims about the same procedure, which is why the TAPP workbooks name them as separate items.

4.title: Number of Replicates
4.description: How many replicates the statistic is based on. Distinct from a procedure-level replicate count: this one qualifies THIS measure, and three replicates behind an RSD is a weaker claim than thirty.
specify the quality measure that is reported, by name, with an ID ref, or as a Defined Term
the reported result of the quality measure, as a string, a number, or a defined term from a vocabulary

5.description: link to appropriate basemap image map
Whether coordinates are stage-defined or pixel-defined. If pixel-defined, are coordinates from stage, upperleftPixel, or centerPixel.
Units of the CRS coordinates, i.e. of originX/Y/Z. A world file carries no units.
The location of the origin pixel of an image. Range: upperLeft, upperRight, lowerLeft, lowerRight, center
CRS x of the origin pixel (world-file C). Which pixel that is, is stated by ada:originLocation rather than assumed to be the upper-left.
CRS y of the origin pixel (world-file F).
CRS z of the origin pixel, where the registration is to a three-dimensional frame. A world file has no equivalent, and a planar thin section does not need one.

The x-component of one ROW step (world-file B): how far CRS x moves per row, which is zero when the image axes are parallel to the sample axes. Non-zero whenever the stage was rotated relative to the sample frame -- the case a scale-and-origin model cannot express at all, which is why both off-diagonal terms are declared here rather than assumed away.

The y-component of one COLUMN step (world-file D): how far CRS y moves per column, zero for an axis-aligned image. Optional, and absent means zero, so a registration that omits both rotation terms is the axis-aligned case -- which is what every record carries today.
CRS units per column step (world-file A).
CRS units per row step (world-file E). A world file conventionally makes this NEGATIVE to encode the y-axis flip; here the sense is carried by ada:originLocation, so this is a magnitude.
Units of ada:pixelScaleX/Y, e.g. nm, um, mm. Normalise before comparing values.

Link to an EXTERNAL world file that carries the affine transform, instead of stating the six parameters inline -- a .tfw beside a GeoTIFF, an ESRI .wld, or any sidecar of that form. Use it when the transform already exists as a file the instrument or the processing software wrote: restating those numbers by hand is a second copy that can disagree with the first, and the file is the authority.
A record states the transform ONE way or the other, which the anyOf below enforces: either the inline parameters (origin, scales, corner, coordinate definition) or this reference. Both together is permitted and is not recommended -- nothing can adjudicate a disagreement between them, and the inline copy is the one that goes stale.
READ THE DEPARTURES BELOW BEFORE TRUSTING A ROUND TRIP. A world file is not quite what this object says, so importing one into the inline terms, or writing one out from them, needs the sign and the unit handled deliberately rather than copied.

6.description: Ordered list of cdi:ComponentPosition wrappers. Each wrapper carries cdi:indexes (an @id-reference to a cdi:InstanceVariable declared elsewhere in the dataset) and cdi:value (the 1-based integer position in the key).

The variable this position indexes -- an @id-reference to one declared elsewhere in the document. At dataset level (cdif:hasPrimaryKey) that is a cdi:InstanceVariable in schema:variableMeasured; at data-structure level (cdif:has_PrimaryKey, cdif:has_ForeignKey) it is a cdi:RepresentedVariable in the structure. The value is a bare objectReference either way: a key names variables that are defined once and referenced from the key, so an inline variable here would be a second copy of a node that already exists.

1-based position of this variable in the ordered key. Pinned to a minimum of 1 because a key that might be 0- or 1-based has ambiguous ordering, which defeats the purpose of recording a position at all -- and because both structure-level key definitions already rejected 0, so the latitude this description used to advertise was never honoured anywhere.

properties.title: Analysis Events
properties.description: Analysis events. Extends cdifProvActivity (from cdifProvenance) with the generic geochem analysis-event surface: the instruments, computational tools and reagents actually used (schema:instrument); the laboratory; the samples analysed (schema:object); the TAPP the analysis followed (schema:actionProcess); and the session identifier and timing.

The TAPP this analysis event followed, or the workflow as it was performed.
Two forms, after the CDIF plan link (cdifProvActivity; option A of the 2026-11-11 activity-used-resources proposal). A bare {"@id": ...} is the link to the TAPP definition, which is typed schema:HowTo for exactly this reason. An inline schema:HowTo is the workflow as performed; when the event also followed a TAPP, that HowTo names it with schema:isBasedOn. One path finds the TAPP either way: prov:wasGeneratedBy/schema:actionProcess/schema:isBasedOn?. The TAPP link used to be the role-keyed prov:used wrapper {"ada:tappDefinition": {...}}, which is closed off below. Inline TAPPs are not accepted here: none existed in ada2 or ada_subjects when the link moved (measured 2026-11-11), so the reference is the only form.
The reference is SEALED, as the ada:tappDefinition reference was, and so is schema:isBasedOn: a TAPP link names the plan and says nothing else about it.
The base cdifProvActivity already supplies a schema:HowTo here, but its step shape carries only @type / name / description / position / url. A geochem analysis event needs the same step surface the TAPP plan uses -- per-step instruments, computational tools and reagents (schema:instrument), inputs (schema:object), result, parameters and sub-workflow -- so the step items are pinned to tappDefinition's WorkflowStep. Both apply: the base and this intersect under allOf, and neither the base HowTo nor its step is a closed object, so the richer shape adds to it rather than conflicting.
WorkflowStep, NOT WorkflowHowTo, is deliberate. The requirement for exactly one "Sample preparation" step carrying bios:LabProcess lives on WorkflowHowTo, and it belongs to the TAPP plan -- a protocol must say how the sample was prepared. An analysis EVENT records what was done and may legitimately describe only part of a workflow, so referencing the step shape alone brings the structure without that requirement.
The TAPP definition this workflow was based on, by reference.
Name of this workflow step (e.g. "Sample preparation").
Detailed description of what this step involves.
Ordinal position in the workflow sequence (1-based).

Further classification of this step (e.g. bios:LabProcess for wet-lab steps, schema:CreateAction for production steps). A CURIE may also be written as a JSON-LD IRI reference, which is what CDIF's schemaorgProperties/additionalProperty SHACL asks for; the `contains` on the method's schema:step accepts either serialization, so widening here cannot orphan the sample-preparation requirement.

The instruments, computational tools and reagents used in this step, as on the plan: each item one of the three kinds (see PlanResource), or a sealed {@id} reference to one described elsewhere -- typically an instrument the plan already describes. Always an array; a single instrument object was accepted here until 2026-11-11.
Superseded: a computational tool is a schema:instrument item of the software kind (Wikidata Q7397). Move it there.
Superseded: a reagent is a schema:instrument item of the reagent kind (Wikidata Q2356542). Move it there.
Superseded: a step's inputs are schema:object. Move them there.
Output entity produced by this step (can be referenced as input by a subsequent step).

The input(s) of this step: a reference to a prior step whose result is the input (action chaining), or the entities it consumed or referenced (e.g. a prepared sample). One value or an array of them, each a string or a sealed {@id} reference -- the shape the step's prov:used inputs had before they moved here on 2026-11-11.

Step-specific parameters (e.g. beam conditions for the acquisition step, matrix correction settings for the data processing step). Editable parameters are schema:PropertyValueSpecification entries (a default the analyst may override); read-only parameters are schema:PropertyValue entries carrying the fixed protocol value.
Machine-readable parameter name for serialization (e.g. "acceleratingVoltage").
Guidance text shown to the user in the form.

Controlled vocabulary providing allowed values for this parameter. When present, form renders a dropdown/select populated from the vocabulary. Four shapes are accepted: (1) a plain URI string identifying an external SKOS ConceptScheme; (2) an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere; (3) a LabeledLink (LinkRole with name and URL); (4) an inline schema:DefinedTermSet enumerating the allowed values
    as schema:DefinedTerm objects (replaces the prior ada:enumeration).

Role of the related resource. Present only on a link that expresses a relationship; a plain labeled link such as a license omits it.
DCAT's declared range is dcat:Role (dcat.ttl: rdfs:range dcat:Role, and dcat:Role rdfs:subClassOf skos:Concept), so the DCAT-native form is a node typed dcat:Role. That form was NOT accepted here before 2026-10-01: this property was cdifConceptOrTermOrString alone, which matches a bare string, a sealed @id reference, a schema:DefinedTerm or a skos:Concept -- none of which a dcat:Role-typed node satisfies, because JSON Schema does no subclass reasoning.
dcat:Role is added as a branch rather than replacing the others, so the DCAT-native form becomes valid without invalidating anything already written. Note this leaves CDIF LOOSER than DCAT, deliberately: DCAT's range is dcat:Role alone, and CDIF also accepts a plain skos:Concept, a DefinedTerm, an @id reference and a string. That is the same both-forms stance taken on dcterms:relation, and it is a choice rather than an oversight -- do not read the extra branches as something not yet tightened.

The related resource -- the DCAT canonical pointer to what is being related to, which is distinct from schema:url, the presentation URL of the link itself.
An @id reference is the RECOMMENDED form and a string is permitted, which is DCMI's own position: "Recommended practice is to identify the related resource by means of a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a string conforming to a formal identification system may be provided." DCMI declares no rdfs:range for this property, and of the 13 DCMI properties carrying an "intended to be used with non-literal values" restriction, this is deliberately not one. dcat.ttl does not re-declare or constrain it at all -- the only triple mentioning it in the whole DCAT vocabulary is `dcat:distribution rdfs:subPropertyOf dcterms:relation`.
So objectReference-only would be stricter than both DCAT and DCMI and would reject a form the specification sanctions. The anyOf matches how schema:additionalType is handled here: both forms valid, the object form used in examples and required only where a `contains` pins a specific value.
It was string-only until 2026-10-01, which rejected the @id form outright. Reported from outside by a PSDI validator taking a things-not-strings approach (profile-core#16): their DCAT catalogue mirrors the DCAT-3 spec examples and wrote {"@id": ...}, which failed both layers -- while CDIF's own documented URI serialization policy (agents.md) says URI values SHOULD be {"@id": ...}. The register required the one form its own policy argues against.
The default value for this parameter. For constant parameters (readonlyValue=true), this is the fixed value. For editable parameters, this is the pre-filled default.
true = constant, fixed for every session (read-only in form). false = editable (default or optional depending on valueRequired).
true = must be provided (mandatory). false = optional. Combined with readonlyValue: readonly+required = constant mandatory; !readonly+required = editable mandatory; !readonly+!required = optional.
Minimum allowed numeric value. Defines the lower bound of a valid range at the method level; specific values within this range may be set per element in ada:targetSpeciesTemplate.
Maximum allowed numeric value. Upper bound of valid range.
Granularity expected of the value (e.g. 0.1 for nA).
Regex pattern for validating string values.
Whether multiple values are allowed (default false).
Whether this parameter is fixed at the method level, varies per analytical session, or is element-specific.
Grouping label for form layout (e.g. "Beam Conditions", "Data Processing", "Quality Control"). String for simple cases; DefinedTerm to link to a controlled vocabulary of parameter categories.
Expected data type for the parameter value.
URI for unit of measure (QUDT preferred).
The CDIF building block property path this parameter maps to. Used for JSON-LD serialisation.
Mandatory / Recommended / Optional tier from the metadata profile. Informs validation strictness.
The fixed protocol value for this read-only parameter.

Sub-workflow for this step, expressed as a nested schema:HowTo with its own ordered steps. Use for steps that have a multi-phase internal procedure (e.g. sample preparation with mount, grind, polish, coat).
Name of the workflow (e.g. "EPMA WDS analytical workflow").
Overview of the workflow.
URL to a published protocol document.

Ordered sequence of workflow steps. Each step is a schema:Action + schema:HowToStep describing a distinct phase of the analytical procedure. This shape carries NO sample-preparation requirement, because it is used for a STEP's sub-workflow as well as for a method's top-level workflow; see MethodWorkflowHowTo for the method form that does require one.
Quality measurements specific to this workflow step.

properties.title: Resources Used
properties.description: What the analysis used, other than its samples: the instruments, the computational tools actually used (acquisition, reduction, processing) and the reagents and reference materials actually used. One array, the kinds told apart by the Wikidata term each item carries in schema:additionalType -- Q3099911 (measuring instrument), Q7397 (software), Q2356542 (chemical reagent) -- which is the CDIF cdifProvActivity rule. Each item is one of those, or a sealed {@id} reference (the CDIF base admits both, and requires exactly one kind term on an item described in place). The TAPP plan prescribes the generic instruments, tools and reagents; these record the ACTUALS used in this specific run.
Carries the Wikidata kind term, https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q7397 (software), as {"@id": ...}: what makes this a software item of the activity's schema:instrument.
Formal identifier (IGSN, catalog number, GeoReM ID).
Registry code for the material on the schema:DefinedTerm path.
The registry the schema:termCode belongs to.

Not where this profile records what an analysis used: instruments, tools and reagents are schema:instrument, samples are schema:object, and the TAPP link is schema:actionProcess. A prov:used that passes the CDIF core shape (strings and @id references) is accepted and checked by nothing more.
The superseded spellings are CLOSED OFF, so a writer that regressed to one fails, naming the key, instead of passing silently. The role-keyed wrappers carry no @id and the CDIF core rejects them already; these close them off by name, and close off the one old form that does carry an @id -- an item typed ada:TAPPDefinition. Same sequence as the earlier close-offs: the records move first (the ADA stores are migrated before this is published), then the schema.
Superseded wrapper: an instrument is an item of the activity's own schema:instrument.
Superseded wrapper: a computational tool is a schema:instrument item of the software kind (Wikidata Q7397).
Superseded wrapper: a reagent is a schema:instrument item of the reagent kind (Wikidata Q2356542).
Superseded twice over (prov:reagent, then bios:reagent): a reagent is a schema:instrument item of the reagent kind.
Superseded wrapper: the TAPP link is schema:actionProcess {"@id": ...}, or schema:isBasedOn on the event's inline workflow.

properties.description: Samples analyzed
Sample name/identifier as used in the lab.
Per-sample PropertyValue entries (e.g. analysis location); technique profiles constrain these.

properties.title: Spatial Registration
properties.description: The coordinate system defined ON the sample -- typically a planar thin section -- that image pixel coordinates are registered to. Distinct from the ada:spatialRegistration on an image or imageMap part, which maps pixel coordinates WITHIN one file: this one is the frame those are registered to, and is what lets two images of the same section be compared. Optional, and no record carries it yet.

properties.title: Session Identifier
properties.description: The analytical session's own identifier -- the laboratory's run, sequence or batch identifier as generated by the instrument or acquisition software. Sits on the activity rather than the dataset because the session IS the activity.
Superseded: the analysis start is schema:startTime. Rename the key.
Superseded: the analysis end is schema:endTime. Rename the key.
Per-analysis PropertyValue entries (replicates, transect length, ...); technique profiles constrain these.

The reported values this session obtained by averaging or otherwise combining several individual results -- the ROWS of the combined-result table, and the domain that `defines: combined result` enumerates (Rule 7; see the Legends sheet of any delivered TAPP). One entry per combined value, each naming what it combines: "Olivine, sample A, 8 points", "Zircon weighted-mean date, sample B, 236 of 246 spots", "Isochron, sample C, 36 runs".
On the ACTIVITY rather than on a sample, because a combined result names its own sample and need not belong to exactly one -- an isochron over 36 runs is the case in hand.
It is METADATA, unlike a sampling unit, and the difference is worth being clear about because an earlier design got it wrong. A combined result is a statement the record makes about its own contents, so it belongs here. An individual sampling unit is not: the procedure and the analysis can state only the KIND of unit (ada:samplingUnitType), while a particular unit's identifier is a schema:variableMeasured naming a COLUMN in one of the distributions, and the binding from that unit to its target material exists only in the instance data table beside the results. There is therefore no array of sampling-unit objects here; one was added on 2026-09-25 and removed on 2026-10-01 once that was settled.
Analysis-side only: the procedure can say HOW results will be combined (Combination Method, keyed by reported property) but not WHICH were, so there is no ada:combinedResults counterpart in tappDefinition.
Fields keyed `combined result x reported property` -- Goodness-of-Fit or Dispersion Statistic, and Other Statistics -- ride on these rows as per-reported- property values, keyed by the valueName of the column that declared them.
What this combined value is and what it combines. Required, because a combined result nothing can name gives a field keyed by combined result no row to attach its value to.

The RepresentedVariable this InstanceVariable instantiates. A reference only (@id, nothing else): the point of the link is that the represented-variable-level properties are defined once on the RepresentedVariable and NOT duplicated here, so an inline copy would defeat it. The equivalent link within a data structure is cdif:isDefinedBy_Variable on cdifDataStructureComponent -- a different name because it means something wider: it accepts an InstanceVariable as well (in DDI-CDI an InstanceVariable IS a RepresentedVariable), and accepts one inline, because a structure may define a variable that exists nowhere else. This property stays narrow: the RepresentedVariable an InstanceVariable instantiates, by reference.

Essentially the same as schema:propertyID. References the concept(s) this variable measures or represents -- and nothing else. A RepresentedVariable is NOT a legal value: that link is cdif:isDefinedBy_RepresentedVariable, which is reference-only and carries the no-duplication rule. The RepresentedVariable branch was removed 2026-09-25. It never widened what could be *written*, because cdifConceptOrTerm's first branch is already a sealed {@id} reference, so it only ever admitted an inline RepresentedVariable node -- which framing produced and nothing authored. Keeping it cost the property its single value type, made it a partial exception to the CDIF convention of disambiguating polymorphic DDI-CDI role names by target, and left it not type-compatible with canonical cdi:uses, which is valued by a Concept. The RepresentedVariable branch is not new behaviour: it is what the rest of CDIF already documents and enforces. description.md calls cdif:uses "concepts (or, under the Data Structure profile, the RepresentedVariable)"; agents.md describes the InstanceVariable as "a pointer (via cdif:uses) into a richer RepresentedVariable"; the six NoDuplicate*Shape rules in cdifDataStructure traverse cdif:uses to reach that RepresentedVariable; and RepresentedVariableMustBeInstantiatedShape requires the link to exist. Only this schema said Concepts-only, and it was the outlier -- documents conforming to those rules could not be expressed here. A bare {@id} always matched via cdifConceptOrTerm; the branch is needed for the embedded form, because framing inlines a node whose @id is defined in the same document. cdif:isDefinedBy_RepresentedVariable remains the way to say that this InstanceVariable DEFERS its represented-variable-level properties to that RepresentedVariable; it is reference-only and carries the exclusivity rule. The cost is that cdif:uses no longer has a single value type, so it is a partial exception to the CDIF convention of disambiguating polymorphic DDI-CDI role names by target, and no longer strictly type-compatible with canonical cdi:uses, which is valued by a Concept.

How masses are assigned to collector positions for this procedure, AS THE SOURCE STATES IT. Free text on purpose: submitters write this as prose or as a semicolon-separated list in no agreed syntax ("L3=116Sn (Sn); L2=117Sn (Sn); Ax=120Sn ..."), and in many cases it cannot be parsed at all. Recording the statement verbatim is what can always be done; ada:collectors below is what can sometimes be done as well. Meaningful on a component whose schema:additionalType includes 'Collector'.

The collector table. One member per position when ada:collectorConfiguration parses into positions, and ONE member carrying the text as written when it does not -- the N=1 form of the flattening fallback that TAPP-keyed-values-design.md Decision 6 settles for every keyed axis: "rather than admit two shapes, always emit the table: a declaration that does not parse into members yields a one-row table whose row key is the text as written. The fallback is then not a separate branch but N=1."
So a consumer reads one shape either way. In the N=1 form schema:name is a fixed label rather than a cup ('Collector configuration description'), schema:description carries the unparsed string, and the per-item values ride in schema:additionalProperty as name/value pairs. Parsing these strings to individual collectors is not tractable in general -- they are written for a person to read -- so N=1 is expected to be the common case, not the exception.
This exists because a cup label has to be referenceable WHEN there is one. A per-cup quantity (a baseline, a gain factor) and a monitored property that names the position reporting it both need something to point AT, and a label buried in a sentence is not something a consumer can join to. schema:name is that anchor.
What a collector does NOT carry is which monitored property it measures. That assignment is procedure configuration, not hardware -- the same physical array is wired differently by another procedure, and an analysis may override it -- so it lives as the 'collector' column of ada:monitoredPropertyColumns on the method definition, whose values are these schema:names. Putting it here would invert the dependency and make the instrument description procedure-specific.
Note what an N=1 member does NOT assert: it names no cup, so it makes no per-cup claim. That matters because the resistor values are attested per MASS, not per cup (Proposal_Monitored_Property_2026-09-10 §10), and the fallback must not quietly move them onto the collector axis.

The collector position label as the instrument names it -- L5..L1, C or Ax, H1..H5, IC1..IC8 on a Neptune-class multicollector. This is the identifier other properties reference. In the N=1 fallback there is no position to name, so it is the fixed label 'Collector configuration description' and nothing should join to it.

Quantities carried on this member as name/value pairs. In the parsed form these are per-position quantities that cannot be restated per mass -- a baseline, a gain factor. In the N=1 form they are the source fields themselves, each as its item name and the text as written, which is how an unparseable per-collector statement is preserved without inventing an assignment it does not make.
